newsitem.title: USA: American Oilfield insured on sunk vessel.
newsitem.headline: American Oilfield insured on sunk vessel.

text.p: American Oilfield Divers Inc said Monday that it is insured on the vessel and the crane which sunk in the Gulf of Mexico on Sunday.

Its American Marine Construction division announced on Monday that the AMERICAN INTREPID (also known as the Pool Ranger IV), a 150-foot converted jackup derrick barge on time-charter from Pool Company, sunk in 50 feet of water seven miles off Grand Isle, Louisiana.

The vessel was engaged in an operation to salvage parts of a disused oil platform when it began to list Sunday morning. When the listing reached three degrees the vessel was abandoned and later sank, said Greg Rosenstein, a spokesman for AOD.
The crane on board the vessel belonged to AOD.

"We do have insurance on the vessel and the crane but that's all pending investigation," said Rosenstein. The Coast Guard, the company and other authorities were looking into the cause. At the time, the crane on board was not lifting any material, Rosenstein said.
He decliend to identify the company's insurance company, saying AOD preferred any claimants to contact AOD directly rather than the insurance company.
